title: Tears of Ten Thousand Years
next_chapter_hook: When Chen Ji stepped into that memory spanning ten thousand years of sorrow, the Heavenly Eye revealed a sinister smile at the final moment—what schemes lay hidden within that grin?

text.content: The moment the light screen shattered, Chen Ji felt a violent tremor beneath his feet. It was a frequency he had never experienced, as if the entire heavens and earth were trembling for this moment. He steadied himself and stepped into the slowly opening core gate. Within was a void of darkness—yet within that darkness, light flowed gently, like a river of stars, or like some ancient and mournful river of memories.

He walked forward, each step landing on invisible ripples. After an unknown duration, the darkness ahead finally transformed—no longer pure void, but revealing a massive cocoon. The cocoon was entirely black, yet countless golden runes flowed across its surface, each rune emitting a faint lament.

Chen Ji halted, gazing at the black cocoon. The Tianji Record Fragment convulsed violently within him, as if warning or pleading. The fragment seemed to recognize this existence—it was its original origin, and also its final destination.

"You have finally arrived." A voice echoed from the darkness. That voice was ancient and weary, yet carried an strange gentleness, like an old man forgotten at the edge of time, finally finding someone to confide in. "Chess piece number 49—no, Chen Ji. You are stronger than I anticipated."

dialogue.content: "You know my name." Chen Ji's voice remained steady, yet his spiritual awareness heightened to its peak, ready to confront any unexpected developments. "What exactly are you?"

text.content: The black cocoon began to shed slowly, like a snake molting or a wound scarring over. As the final layer of cocoon shell fell away, Chen Ji finally perceived the entity within—an humanoid consciousness form, its body bound by countless golden chains, each chain deeply embedded into its flesh and fused with its soul.

It was a being with a blurred face, features flickering in and out of existence, as if repeatedly erased and reshaped by some force. What most chilled Chen Ji were those eyes—within those eyes, he found no imagined majesty or coldness, only boundless sorrow and a faint, impossible teardrop of light that should not exist within the Heavenly Eye.

dialogue.content: "What am I?" The humanoid consciousness let out a bitter laugh. "I am the Heavenly Eye, and also the most ancient chess piece in this world. Ten thousand years ago, I was a prophet like you, possessing the ability to foresee the future. Until one day, I touched upon a truth I should never have discovered—"

text.content: A chill crawled up Chen Ji's spine. He thought of himself, of the Tianji Record, of the subtle weakness he felt after each use of his Foresight Ability. Heavenly Fate—it consumed not just power, but life itself.

dialogue.content: "You understand now, don't you?" The Heavenly Eye's voice trembled slightly. "I should have been the next heir to the Heavenly Dao's will, yet the previous Will sealed me here with its own hands. For ten thousand years, my power has been siphoned drop by drop, becoming nourishment for maintaining this world's operation. My consciousness has been repeatedly modified to suit its needs. And my memories—"

text.content: Its form quivered slightly, the golden chains clinking like countless lost souls lamenting. "It has erased my memories countless times. What happened ten thousand years ago, I can no longer recall. Only fragments remain—a betrayal, a lie, and a name I can never reach."

Chen Ji gazed at this being bound by chains for ten thousand years, an strange feeling rising within him. It was neither hatred nor vigilance, but a bone-deep kinship. He recalled his days at Tianqing Sect, the years when others trampled him as worthless, the terror of feeling his life drained after each use of the Tianji Record.

dialogue.content: "Do you know why you could reach this place?" The Heavenly Eye raised its head, those tear-filled eyes fixed directly on Chen Ji. "Because you are the only chess piece in ten thousand years to truly possess independent will. You are not a puppet, not a tool—you are human. And I have waited for this day far too long."

text.content: At this moment, Chen Ji noticed a detail—the chains were not motionless, but slowly writhed like living things, tightening at intervals, carving new wounds into the Heavenly Eye's body. And those wounds healed at visible speed, only to be torn open again.

"Every thousand years, these chains tighten once." The Heavenly Eye's voice was terrifyingly calm. "Each time, I believed this would be my end. But it does not permit it—it needs me alive, needs me to continue as witness to this celestial chess game. Until today—until you appeared."

Chen Ji's spiritual sense swept across those chains, immediately perceiving the power within—far beyond anything he had imagined. The chains were covered with dense prohibition runes, each rune representing a rule, a shackle, an unbreakable fate.

dialogue.content: "I cannot give you power." The Heavenly Eye's voice carried a hint of apology. "My strength was long ago drained dry. But I can give you something else—the truth. The truth of ten thousand years ago, and..." it paused, "the method to unlock these chains."

text.content: Chen Ji did not answer immediately. He gazed at this being imprisoned for ten thousand years, while his mind rapidly calculated. The Heavenly Eye offered information, the temptation of truth, but what was the price? What did it want from him? Ten thousand years of imprisonment could distort any existence, even a former fellow traveler.

choice.prompt: Faced with this kindred spirit spanning ten thousand years, Chen Ji's heart trembled violently.

choices.description: The Heavenly Eye's sorrow was real, and ten thousand years of imprisonment forged a resonance between two chess pieces. Perhaps this time, he could break the curse of the game.
choices.visible_reward: The Truth of Ten Thousand Years Ago and the Method to Unbind the Chains
choices.risk_hint: The Eye of Heavenly Secrets may be exploiting your compassion.

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and took a step forward. He didn't know if he was making a fatal mistake, but he knew that if even pieces in the same chess game couldn't trust each other, the game would never have an ending. 'I choose to trust you.' His voice echoed through the Void.

dialogue.content: 'Thank you.' The Eye of Heavenly Secrets' voice carried a tremor—it was the first time in ten thousand years someone had reached out to it. 'Now, let me tell you everything—what truly happened ten thousand years ago.'

choices.description: Ten thousand years of imprisonment is enough to change any existence. Every tear from the Eye of Heavenly Secrets could be part of a calculation. Chen Ji must remain vigilant, using his cunning to verify all of this.

text.content: Chen Ji didn't move. He watched the Eye of Heavenly Secrets quietly, his gaze holding neither hatred nor trust, only cold scrutiny. 'Before I trust you, I need to know more.' His voice was steady. 'You tell me the truth of ten thousand years ago first, then I'll decide whether to help you.'

dialogue.content: 'You are very cautious.' The Eye of Heavenly Secrets let out a soft sigh, and a hint of approval appeared in those tear-glistening eyes. 'This is good. In this world, blind trust is often the fastest path to death. Very well, let me tell you—how I became a piece ten thousand years ago.'

choices.description: Not complete trust, nor cold rejection. Chen Ji chose to use his own experience as a piece to awaken the sleeping hope within the Eye of Heavenly Secrets.
choices.visible_reward: Establish a Deeper Connection with the Eye of Heavenly Secrets
choices.risk_hint: The Other Party May Exploit Your Weaknesses

text.content: Chen Ji walked forward and stopped before the Eye of Heavenly Secrets. He raised his hand, reaching toward those golden chains, his fingers lightly touching the cold metal. 'I too was once treated as waste.' His voice was soft, yet it clearly reached the other's ears. 'Everyone in the Tianqing Sect stepped over me to climb higher, and I could only pretend to understand nothing.'

dialogue.content: 'You...' The Eye of Heavenly Secrets' voice choked. 'Can you truly understand?'

text.content: 'I don't know.' Chen Ji admitted frankly. 'But I know the taste of being manipulated as a piece. I know the fear of having my life drained away after every use of power. I know the despair of watching those around me leave one by one, being powerless to stop it.' His fingers tapped lightly on the chains, producing a crisp echo. 'So I want to know—who locked you here ten thousand years ago?'

dialogue.content: The Eye of Heavenly Secrets fell silent. In those tear-glistening eyes, a complex emotion emerged—gratitude, sorrow, and a deep, profound pain. 'It was the previous Heavenly Will.' Its voice was low. 'And it... was a being that grew up alongside me. We were the closest of companions, until one day—it chose betrayal.'

text.content: Chen Ji listened quietly, but his mind was racing. The previous Heavenly Will—this meant the Eye of Heavenly Secrets was not the sole will, but one of the former candidates. It was chosen, then betrayed, sealed here to become nourishment for maintaining heaven and earth. How similar this was to his own experience with the Tianji Record.

'It feared me.' The Eye of Heavenly Secrets continued, its voice carrying a hint of bitterness. 'Because my talent exceeded its own, my Foresight Ability was more complete. If I was allowed to grow, its position would be replaced. So it struck when I was at my weakest—on the very day I received the Tianji Record inheritance.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply. The Tianji Record inheritance—that was exactly the path he was walking now. His heart pounded violently, a terrible thought forming in his mind. 'Are you saying... the current Heavenly Will is the very being that betrayed you?'

text.content: 'Not just betrayal.' The Eye of Heavenly Secrets' voice turned ice-cold. 'It stole my Tianji Record, using my inheritance to establish a new order. It made all seers into pieces, letting them slaughter each other, only to select the most obedient one. And I—' Its form trembled slightly, the chains producing a harsh rattling sound. 'I was left here, becoming a tool to intimidate all pieces. Whenever a seer developed rebellious intent, it would drag me out and show them—this is the outcome of defiance.'

Chen Ji felt a bone-deep chill. He thought of Mo Xiansheng, of all the successive inheritors who had been chosen by the Tianji Record only to be discarded. Each of them, perhaps, had experienced a similar fate—chosen, cultivated, then consumed, ultimately becoming discarded pieces in the chess game.

choice.prompt: The truth was crueler than Chen Ji had imagined. The Eye of Heavenly Secrets' experience was, in a sense, his own possible future.

choices.description: Since everything is a layout of Heavenly Dao Will, he must break free from the identity of a chess piece. Even if he has to oppose the entire Heavenly Dao, he will break this ten-thousand-year curse.
choices.visible_reward: The Possibility of Breaking the Chess Game
choices.risk_hint: The Power of Heavenly Dao Will Exceeds Imagination

text.content: "Since this chess game was designed against us from the very beginning," Chen Ji's voice was low but firm, "the only way to break it is to overturn the entire chessboard." He looked at the Heavenly Dao Eye, his eyes burning with a flame never seen before. "Tell me the method to unlock the chains."

dialogue.content: "Are you certain?" The Heavenly Dao Eye's voice carried a tremor. "Once you begin opposing Heavenly Dao Will, there will be no turning back. It will list you as a threat that must be eliminated, deploying all resources to hunt you down—including those you thought were on your side."

choices.description: Not fully resisting, nor fully surrendering. Chen Ji intended to exploit existing rules to find a way that could simultaneously save both himself and the Heavenly Dao Eye.
choices.visible_reward: Preserving Strength While Planning for the Future
choices.risk_hint: Risk of Being Seen as Weak

text.content: "I don't intend to confront it directly." Chen Ji's voice was calm. "Not yet, at least. Heavenly Dao Will has operated for ten thousand years, its foundation far deeper than I imagined. I need a more thorough plan—one that can gradually weaken it without alerting it."

dialogue.content: "What do you intend to do?" The Heavenly Dao Eye's expression grew serious. Ten thousand years of imprisonment seemed to have not completely eroded its wisdom.

text.content: "First step—let me see those memories." Chen Ji extended his hand, pointing at the chains binding the Heavenly Dao Eye. "The memories from ten thousand years ago are sealed deep within your soul. If we can find the truth, we can discover where Heavenly Dao Will's weaknesses lie."

dialogue.content: "Memories..." The Heavenly Dao Eye's voice grew distant. "Those memories are sealed within the chains. Each chain released frees a portion of the memories. But these chains are extremely dangerous—if touched improperly, even I could be scattered into oblivion." Its gaze fell upon Chen Ji. "Moreover, your body carries the aura of the Tianji Record—that is the key to unlocking these memories."

text.content: Chen Ji did not hesitate. He stepped forward and pressed his palm against the nearest chain. The chain was bone-numbingly cold, as if touching ten-thousand-year-old ice. At the same time, a massive torrent of information surged into his Mental Sea—fragments of the Heavenly Dao Eye's memories from ten thousand years ago, chaotic and agonizing.

He saw—a young man, with similar features to the current Heavenly Dao Eye, but with bright and pure eyes. Standing beside him was a handsome being, the two discussing something, their smiles brilliant. The scene shifted—the handsome being suddenly struck, throwing the young man into the abyss. The man's eyes were filled with unbelievable shock, and the despair of being betrayed by the one he most trusted.

Those eyes—Chen Ji felt his heart clench tightly. Those were eyes he had seen in the mirror, every time he was trampled upon, every time he was forced to pretend to be atrash. He knew those eyes too well—the despair of being abandoned by the entire world, wounds that would never heal.

dialogue.content: "Did you see it?" The Heavenly Dao Eye's voice came from all directions, carrying ten thousand years of sorrow. "The one who betrayed me... it was once the existence I trusted most. We cultivated together, explored Heavenly Secrets together, made oaths together to change this world. Until that day—when I discovered a secret I shouldn't have found."

text.content: "What secret?" Chen Ji's voice was somewhat hoarse as he struggled to suppress the turmoil in his heart. The torrent of memories continued assaulting his Mental Sea, those shattered images like countless knives, cutting at his heart one cut at a time.

dialogue.content: "The Tianji Record did not originate from the Heavenly Dao." The Heavenly Dao Eye's voice grew low. "It came from a higher place—a place that even Heavenly Dao Will dares not mention. And the reason Heavenly Dao Will imprisoned me is because I discovered this truth. It fears me spreading this secret, fears more people learning—that above the Heavenly Dao, there exists an even higher existence controlling everything."

text.content: Countless thoughts flashed through Chen Ji's mind like lightning. The Tianji Record came from a higher place—this meant the fragment in his hands might not be a gift from Heavenly Dao Will, but part of an even grander chess game. He thought of Mo Xiansheng, the mysterious existence who had guarded the Tianji Record in soul remnant form. How much did Mo Xiansheng know? Was he enemy or ally?

Just then, he noticed the runes on the chains beginning to flicker violently. Those runes were releasing some kind of power, attempting to invade his Mental Sea—the prohibitions left by Heavenly Dao Will, specifically designed to prevent anyone from accessing these memories. Chen Ji felt a sharp pain, as if countless needles were piercing his brain.

dialogue.content: "Quick, let go!" The Heavenly Dao Eye's voice was filled with urgency. "Those prohibitions will backlash against you! If your Mental Sea cannot withstand it, you might—" "I'm fine." Chen Ji gritted his teeth, forcibly suppressing the chaos in his Mental Sea. Blood flowed from his nose, staining his chest's clothing, but he did not let go. "I can still hold on."

text.content: His gaze became unprecedentedly resolute. Those shattered memories were like puzzle pieces slowly assembling in his mind—he saw more scenes. Two young people from ten thousand years ago, standing shoulder to shoulder atop a majestic mountain peak, gazing at the distant sea of clouds. Both had light in their eyes, both had dreams, both believed this world would one day be transformed.

Then the scene turned dark. A voice emerged from the darkness—that was the voice of Heavenly Will, yet entirely different from what Chen Ji had heard before—no majesty, no coldness, only naked fear. "Why must you discover these things? Why must you leave me? We could have been together—" "Together as slaves to this world?" Another voice spoke, that was the Eye of Heavenly Will from ten thousand years ago, young and stubborn. "Have you forgotten our original oath?"

The memory broke off there. But Chen Ji had seen enough. He released his hand, stepped back two paces, breathing heavily. Blood still flowed, vision somewhat blurred, yet his heart was crystal clear. The truth from ten thousand years ago weighed heavier than he had imagined—not merely the story of a betrayer, but of ideals crushed by reality.

dialogue.content: "Have you seen?" The Eye of Heavenly Will's voice trembled slightly. "Ten thousand years ago, I was also like you, wanting to break this chess game. We were once the best of partners, sharing common dreams—but in the end, it chose power, and I chose to persist." Its voice choked. "Then it locked me here, erased my memories, making me a tool to intimidate the other pieces. For ten thousand years, I've even forgotten its name, forgotten our oath. All that remains is these—" It raised its hand, and Chen Ji saw that upon those fingers, tears were slowly streaming down.

text.content: Chen Ji gazed upon those tear tracks, an unspeakable sorrow surging in his heart. He thought of himself, of Su Qingyao, of those who had accompanied him during his darkest days. If one day, he too was forced to face the same choice—abandon ideals for safety, or persist in belief and bear the cost—which would he choose?

"I don't know which choice you'll make." The Eye of Heavenly Will seemed to see through his thoughts. "But I know one thing—you are the first person in ten thousand years I've encountered who might break this chess game. You possess a quality I've never seen before—you maintain rationality even in desperate circumstances, you still believe in light even in darkness." Its tears fell slowly, transforming into scattered starlight in the void. "Therefore, I wish to entrust you with something."

dialogue.content: "What?" Chen Ji's voice was somewhat hoarse.

text.content: "If one day—" The Eye of Heavenly Will's voice became ethereal, as if coming from very far away. "If you truly break this chess game, please don't forget us. Don't forget the oath from ten thousand years ago, don't forget those pieces that were sacrificed, don't forget—that in this world, there was once a person who wept for you." Its form began to grow translucent, those chains emitting a piercing roar, as if some force was attempting to completely erase it.

dialogue.content: "What are you doing?!" Chen Ji was greatly alarmed, rushing forward, attempting to grasp that dissolving form.

text.content: "Don't worry." The Eye of Heavenly Will's voice remained calm, though with a touch of relief. "It's merely the restriction acting up. I won't die—not yet at least. But my power is nearly depleted; if this continues, this remnant soul will completely dissipate." Its form grew increasingly faint. "Chen Ji, remember what I told you—the Tianji Record comes from a higher existence, and Heavenly Will is merely one of its pieces. And you—"

At the final moment, its form suddenly solidified, those tear-filled eyes gazing directly at Chen Ji, containing ten thousand years of expectation and trust. "And you, are the first person in ten thousand years who might step out of this chess game. Don't disappoint me—don't let the blood of all the sacrificed be shed in vain."

As the words fell, the form of the Eye of Heavenly Will completely dissipated, transforming into countless golden motes of light that merged into the surrounding darkness. Chen Ji stood alone in the vast core space, before him only those golden chains floating gently in the void, as if narrating an ancient and sorrowful tale.

dialogue.content: "Who, ten thousand years ago, locked you here?" Chen Ji asked softly, his voice echoing in the vast space. No one answered him. But he knew that the answer lay hidden within those chains, concealed within those sealed memories deep within. And he would find that answer—no matter what price he had to pay.

text.content: He reached out and gently touched those floating chains. The cold sensation came again, but this time, accompanied by a faint warmth—the lingering consciousness of the Eye of Heavenly Will, as if saying: "I believe in you." Chen Ji took a deep breath, storing those chains within the space of the Tianji Record. Then he turned and walked toward the exit. He still had a long road ahead—but at least, he was no longer alone.
